doc: Shared conformance fixtures for the engine-authority rule set (architecture/boundary-rules.json). test/boundary-rules.test.ts runs them through tools/guardrails/boundary.ts (the repository guardrail) and cli/tests/Limen.Core.Tests/BoundaryRulesTests.fs runs them through cli/Limen.Core/Boundary.fs (consumer `limen verify`). Each case lists every (rule, token) expected, in rule-set order; both implementations must produce exactly that list.

cases.name: a browser global in TypeScript engine code
a comment naming the browser is prose, not access
cases.source:
// the engine never touches document or window
export const f = (n: number) => n;

cases.name: a block comment naming the browser is prose
cases.source:
/* uses no window at all */
export const f = (n: number) => n;

cases.name: a string literal naming the browser is data
cases.source:
export const label = "document";
export const other = 'window';

cases.name: a word that contains a token is not the token
cases.source: const documentation = 1; const windowWidth = 2; const fetcher = 3;

cases.name: a call is a call with whitespace before the parenthesis
a template substitution is code
template text is data
nested braces inside a template substitution stay code
a dynamic import acquires a module at run time
an engine may not import a host module
cases.source:
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
export const r = readFile;

cases.name: a side-effect import of a host module is still an import
a comment mentioning a host module is not an import
cases.source:
// never import from "node:fs" here
export const x = 1;

cases.name: the kernel may import host modules
cases.source:
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
export const r = readFile;

cases.name: every TypeScript browser global is caught
cases.source: const a = globalThis; const b = new XMLHttpRequest(); const c = indexedDB; const d = new WebSocket(u); const e = new EventSource(u); postMessage(1); importScripts(u); const f = localStorage; const g = sessionStorage; const h = window;

cases.name: a qualified browser global is still the global
any is a type escape in engine code
any in prose is not a type
cases.source:
// callers may pass any number
export const f = (n: number) => n;

cases.name: the kernel may use the browser
eval is an escape hatch on the kernel side too
an escaped quote does not hide what follows
F# engine code may not open the filesystem
cases.source:
module Domain
open System.IO
let read path = File.ReadAllText path

cases.name: a longer name that starts like a token is not the token
document is ordinary F# domain vocabulary
a qualified F# browser binding is caught
an F# type parameter is not a string
an F# block comment is prose
cases.source:
(* would use HttpClient here *)
let x = 1

cases.name: the F# multiplication operator is not a comment
cases.source:
let m = (*) 2 3
let c = new HttpClient()

cases.name: an F# triple-quoted string is data
F# JavaScript interop is caught
C# engine code may not reach the network
dynamic is a type escape in C# engine code
window is ordinary C# domain vocabulary
cases.source: class D { string Name(Window window) => window.Name; }

cases.name: a C# character literal holding a quote does not open a string
cases.source: class D { char q = '"'; object c = new HttpClient(); }

cases.name: a C# escape hatch is caught on the kernel side
cases.source: class H { void R(IJSRuntime js) => js.SetInnerHtml("x"); }

cases.name: Rust engine code may not bind the browser
a Rust lifetime is not a string
cases.source: pub fn f<'a>(x: &'a str) -> String { std::fs::read_to_string(x).unwrap() }

cases.name: Rust kernel code may bind the browser
a file in no checked language is not scanned
